# Sonos (`sonos`)

Sonos speakers on the local network: volume, mute, night mode, play and pause. A subwoofer can be added read-only.

Generated from the manifest of `plugins/sonos`. The plugin's own manuals: [README](../../../../plugins/sonos/README.md) (what it supports, setup) and [DEVELOPING](../../../../plugins/sonos/DEVELOPING.md) (protocol notes, sources).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Version | 0.1.0 |
| Plugin API | 1 |
| Reaches | local network |
| Classes | `speaker` |
| Config version | 1 |
| More than one instance | no |
| Guided setup | yes |

## What it reaches

- HTTP to the device, port 1400

Nothing at all while the hub is in dry-run.

## Settings

| Key | Label | Kind | Required | Default | Help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `speakers` | Speakers | a list of rows | yes |  | One row per speaker. |
| `speakers[].id` | Id | text, at most 64 | yes |  | A short id for the speaker, such as sonos or sub. It never changes once the speaker is added. |
| `speakers[].url` | Address | URL (http) | yes |  | http://<IP address>:1400. Use the IP address: a Sonos speaker refuses a request addressed by name. |
| `speakers[].read_only` | Read only | true or false | no | `false` | Only read this speaker and never command it. For a subwoofer, which has no playback of its own. |

## Secrets

None.

None: it offers the standard actions of its classes.
